newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq stocks end higher, led by big techs.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq stocks end higher, led by big techs.

text.p: Nasdaq stocks ended higher on Friday, getting a lift from fractional gains by large-capitalization high technology stocks.

Traders said the market ended the week on a generally cautious tone, with investors not willing to place large bets heading into next week's heavy load of economic data including April retail sales, wholesale and retail inflation.
The Nasdaq composite finished up about four points at 1335 with gainers beating losers by a 24-to-17 ratio. For the week the composite rose 30 points, or a 2.3 percent.

"There's a fair amount of strength in the techs," said Brett Discher, vice president of equity trading at Dain Bosworth. Microsoft Corp rose 3/8 to 116-3/4, Intel Corp gained 3/4 to 159-1/2 and Cisco Systems Inc rose 1/4 o 61-5/8.

Elsewhere, Cephalon Inc fell seven to 13 and Chiron Corp shed fell 7/8 to 19-1/8 following a U.S. Food and Drug Administration advisory panel vote to reject the companies' Myotrophin drug for Lou Gehrig's Disease.
Premier Laser Systems Inc rose three to 14 after a 2-5/8-point gain Thursday following the FDA's approval the company's laser system for treating tooth decay.
